references.text: The same command to tear down altars, smash sacred pillars, and cut down Asherah poles is given in connection with the covenant at Sinai
Moses repeats the command to destroy pagan altars, sacred pillars, and Asherah poles when Israel enters Canaan
Command to tear down altars, smash sacred pillars, burn Asherah poles, and destroy the names of idols
Israel was warned against making a covenant with the inhabitants of Canaan and ordered to tear down their altars
Gideon receives the command to tear down Baal's altar and cut down the Asherah pole beside it
During Rehoboam's reign, Judah built high places, sacred pillars, and Asherah poles in violation of God's command
King Hezekiah removed the high places, smashed the sacred pillars, and cut down the Asherah pole in obedience to this command
King Asa removed foreign altars and high places, smashed the sacred pillars, and cut down the Asherah poles
During Hezekiah's reign, the Israelites tore down the sacred pillars, cut down the Asherah poles, and destroyed the high places and altars
King Josiah purified Judah by tearing down altars, Asherah poles, carved images, and cast idols
Prophetic use of the language of the law to warn of God's judgment over Israel's own idols.
Historical fulfillment of Exodus 34:13 through King Asa's reforms.
Parallel legal provision calling for the total destruction of Canaanite worship before the entry into the land.
Judgment on Israel's own worship using the same language as the law's command.
Prophetic judgment that uses the language of the law to describe Israel's complete downfall.
